problem:
The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 3 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Identifying the Pivot Columns of a Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Non-Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form
examples.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $C$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072258/assets/bbc4e9e0d0497930f434cd3dade35973105401ba72c74690d924c6390d87413d.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $C$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072258/assets/da73e68fe8bc5e6baa8876beb17d702707cb0ad43831f42ecfa45f3a98d43202.png)

Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $2$nd column.

feedback.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $A$ is given below. What are the pivot columns of $A?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 7 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $A$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd and $4$th columns:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 7 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
